title: What In-Sensor Computing Is
definition: In-Sensor Computing: sensors that compute before transmitting.
description:
Strip In-Sensor Computing to its essence and you get sensors that compute before transmitting. Simple to say, civilizational to build.

The path runs through Future Computing Paradigms: first compute pixels understanding, then sensor logistics prototypes, then analog preprocessing operations at scale. Each stage has its own physics, its own economics, and its own failure modes — this database maps all three.

Use the ladder: start with foundations, work through the components and forecasts, run every demo, then attempt the compounded drills. By the final record you will hold a working mental model of sensor hulls, grounded in real research and honest about what remains unknown.

title: Real Research Today: In-Sensor Computing
definition: Today's documented research behind In-Sensor Computing.
description:
The road to In-Sensor Computing is already being paved. Microsoft's Majorana program pursues topological qubits for fault-tolerant quantum computing. Memristor crossbar arrays (HP Labs heritage, Knowm, TetraMem) prototype in-memory computing.

DNA data storage (Microsoft/University of Washington) encodes digital data in synthetic DNA. Together these programs form the compute pixels foundation that In-Sensor Computing will build on — the sensor logistics results, the analog preprocessing methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as sensor logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

t: 2030 — First sensor hulls cloud instances rent compute pixels logic by
title: 2030 — First sensor hulls cloud instances rent compute pixels logic by
definition: 2030 milestone on the In-Sensor Computing roadmap.
description:
First sensor hulls cloud instances rent compute pixels logic by the hour to researchers worldwide.

What must be true first: the compute pixels results have to replicate outside the lab, sensor logistics manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and analog preprocessing operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed compute pixels demonstrations, sensor logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting analog preprocessing uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: In-Sensor Computing
definition: Estimates In-Sensor Computing readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six In-Sensor Computing components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a sensor hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

definition: Simulates In-Sensor Computing operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a In-Sensor Computing installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 21131 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where compute pixels monitoring, sensor logistics redundancy, or analog preprocessing maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: In-Sensor Computing Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for In-Sensor Computing: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for In-Sensor Computing — sensors that compute before transmitting.

Phase 1 — Prove (compute pixels): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (sensor logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (analog preprocessing): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (bandwidth savings): sensor hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and IoT-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
